note: Proof-of-concept pooling across the 9 starter papers only. Production system scales this to all 341+ CBP publications plus live registry data. Where a paper reported a precise mean and SD, that real figure is used directly. Where a paper reported only a range (or only a point estimate), a standard deviation was estimated using a documented heuristic and is flagged 'estimated' in the UI. Pediatric and translation(mm)-based studies are shown for reference but excluded from degree-based adult pooling to avoid mixing incompatible populations/units.

studies.citation: Oakley et al. 2021, J Phys Ther Sci — systematic review, 9 controlled trials
studies.sdMethod: Range/4 heuristic applied to the reported 12–18° pooled trial range (represents between-trial uncertainty in the systematic review's synthesized estimate, not raw patient-level SD)

studies.citation: Oakley et al. 2022, J Phys Ther Sci — case report review, Table 1
studies.sdMethod: Directly reported in the paper's summary table (real patient-level SD, n=45 cases with ARA measurement)

studies.citation: Oakley et al. 2020, J Phys Ther Sci — systematic review, 3 controlled trials
studies.sdMethod: Range/4 heuristic applied to the reported 7–11° pooled trial range (between-trial uncertainty, not raw patient-level SD)

studies.citation: Oakley, Kallan & Harrison 2022, JCC — case report review
studies.sdMethod: No SD or range reported in the source paper. Estimated by applying the SD-to-mean ratio observed in the companion cervical case-report paper (9.7/14.1 ≈ 0.69) to this paper's mean — a transparent proxy, not a measured value

studies.citation: Oakley & Harrison 2018, JCC — systematic review, 7 included papers
studies.sdMethod: No SD or range reported. Estimated using the same case-report SD-to-mean ratio proxy (≈0.69) applied to this paper's mean. Only one usable degree-based data point exists in this 9-paper set for thoracic — shown as a single-study estimate, not a multi-study pool

excludedFromPooling.reason: Pediatric population (avg age 8.8) — kept separate from adult cervical pooling to avoid mixing populations with different baseline physiology and response magnitude. Shown as its own reference point: 25° mean increase, n=11.
Outcome measured in millimeters of lateral translation, not degrees of lordosis — a different biomechanical parameter, not directly poolable with the degree-based studies.
Outcome measured in millimeters of lateral translation, not degrees of kyphosis — not directly poolable with the degree-based thoracic study.
Methodology/reliability paper — validates the measurement technique itself, reports no treatment effect size to pool.
